title: Prompt stabilization lab scratchpad
body:
Notes to self: quick-running personal scratchpad for prompt template experiments and documented failure cases. Mostly noisy — using this to capture patterns, short examples, and heuristics before formalizing into the prompt library.

Primary goals:
- Find stable framing for instruction-following across model variants (quantized vs float)
- Create compact few-shot sets that improve hallucination rate for extraction tasks
- Enumerate repeatable failure modes tied to input distribution or token-budget constraints

High-level hypotheses (to validate):
1) Explicit negative examples (1-shot anti-example) reduce creative hallucination on extraction tasks more than adding a second positive example.
2) Conditioning on output schema (JSON with field types) reduces variance across runs when temperature > 0.4.
3) For long-context summarization, a two-stage prompt (chunk summarization -> hierarchical merge) is more robust than single-shot long-context prompts on 8k models.

Quick templates (iterative):
A. Extraction w/ negative example (compact)
- Instruction: "Extract the following fields from the text. If a field cannot be found, output null exactly as "null". Return JSON only."
- Negative example (1): "Text: 'No phone provided.' -> {"phone": null}"
- Positive example (1): "Text: 'Call me at 415-555-0123.' -> {"phone": "415-555-0123"}"
- Prompt pivot: real_text -> produce JSON
- Notes: works ok on 6-bit quant models; sometimes returns empty strings rather than null — add instruction
  'If missing, use null' explicitly.

B. Instruction-following with explicit output types
- System: "You are a precise assistant. Always label types. Output must be valid JSON with keys: summary (string), keywords (list of strings), confidence (float 0-1)."
- Few-shot: 2 examples (one short doc, one long doc)
- Temperature: 0.0-0.2 recommended in prod; test at 0.5 to surface instability.
- Failure modes: sometimes confidence is returned as "low" (string) — need type enforcement line: 'confidence must be numeric between 0 and 1'.

C. Chain-of-thought suppressed summarization (for hallucination reduction)
- Prompt: "Do NOT provide your chain-of-thought or internal reasoning. Provide result only. If uncertain, say 'insufficient information'."
- Rationale: chain-of-thought leaks increase hallucination in some models during open decoding. Testing across model variants needed.

Few-shot candidate sets (compact, 3 examples total):
- Use diverse failure-style examples (edge cases): missing fields, contradictory dates, nested lists.
- Example labels: E1_missing_field, E2_date_conflict, E3_nested_list
- Keep total tokens of examples < 800 for 8k context models to leave room for user input.

Observed failure modes (log snippets & reproduction notes):
- Failure A: Truncated JSON -> model appends trailing commentary "(I think the answer is... )"
  Repro: temperature 0.0, stop sequence set incorrectly. Fix: add explicit stop token and post-validate JSON.
- Failure B: Numeric types returned as strings ("42" vs 42).
  Repro: occurs more on models with instruction-tuning v1; mitigation: specify "use numeric types only" and include numeric-only examples. Consider a simple post-caster layer.
- Failure C: Hallucinated entity when user text includes ambiguous referent.
  Notes: adding a conservative fallback example ("If referent unclear, say 'ambiguous'") reduces hallucination by ~30% in ad-hoc tests.

Experiment log (short):
- 2026-01-10: Ran extraction template A on model-x-8k-6bit, 200 samples. Null-rate incorrect for 12% -> added explicit null instruction.
- 2026-02-02: Tested B template on model-y-4k, temp 0.3 vs 0.0. At 0.3 saw 18% type errors.
- 2026-02-28: Two-stage summarization prototype (chunk->merge) beats single prompt on Rouge L by +2.1 on internal test set (n=50).

Checklist before promoting to shared prompt library:
- [ ] Add canonical name and short description
- [ ] Add schema validation tests (unit tests + harness)
- [ ] Link to evaluation suites (confluence + test harness)
- [ ] Add recommended runtime params (temperature, max_tokens, stop sequences) per model family
- [ ] Add rollback instructions / fallback model mapping (e.g., if model returns non-JSON -> fallback to model-z with stricter decoding)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is it worth adding a machine-verified JSON post-processor in the serving layer versus relying on prompt engineering? (see JIRA-INFR-2345)
- How do quantization artifacts differ between 6-bit and 4-bit for token-level generation of punctuation/quotes? Need synthetic test to surface tokenization drift.
- Create small benchmark of 200 edge cases for numeric typing — assign to Ethan.

Snippets to copy into tests: (use EXACTLY as-is)
--BEGIN-SNIPPET-EXTRACT--
Instruction: Extract fields: name, email, phone. If missing put null. Output JSON only.
Text: "Candidate: Jordan, no email provided, phone 555-745-1234."
Expected: {"name": "Jordan", "email": null, "phone": "555-745-1234"}
--END-SNIPPET--

--BEGIN-SNIPPET-SCHEMA--
Return schema: {"summary": "string", "keywords": ["string"], "confidence": "number (0-1)"}
--END-SNIPPET--

Slack refs: #prompt-lab, thread ts 1701023456. Quick context in thread: Lina reported type flips on model-y-4k.

If I come back later: first step is to formalize A and B into unit tests, then run across the 3 prioritized model families and record token-level diffs.

Random notes: keep examples human-readable but avoid idioms that models hallucinate on (e.g., don't say "obviously" or "as everyone knows").

Signed off (temporary): Maya — will iterate and then move to /shared_drives/product/prompt-library when stable enough.
